budget.basis: D71 (37.0 kg as built, 37.5 kg design; it replaces D69's 35.0 / 35.5 kg); legs 2 x 10.85 kg (leg.json + D53 stops + the D69 wheel at its listed 3.53 kg + the clamp hardware), body and head 15.3 kg

P1.leg_extra: leg.json 9943 g (published with the stops in)

levers.what: shell panels in 2 mm PETG with 1.6 mm ribs instead of 3 mm (PA6-CF at the ear-pod bosses)
floor tray Rev B: lightening cutouts where nothing bolts and T1 is low (1/8 in stays)
deck Rev B: cutouts outside the lidar, the TM pattern and the intake field
the turret mount plate under the deck at the riser, 6061-T6 0.125 in, pocketed (D59)
deck posts printed hollow (22 mm square, 4 mm walls) instead of solid
compute pallet cutouts under the module between the tie-down and the standoffs
the fuse board (D60) instead of ten inline MINI holders and their leads
the 1 mOhm shunt on the fuse board instead of the 85 g Blue Sea 150 A block
the main path in 10 AWG, the VESC leads in 14 AWG, lengths cut to P0's measurements
Pololu D42V110F12 instead of the DDR-60L-12: moot since D65 (the TRACO TEP 150 replaced the DDR-60L-12)
cheeks Rev B: lightening holes where S1 < 40 MPa (-150), or 1/8 in with more standoffs (-330)
aluminium M5 x 120 hex standoffs in place of the printed deck posts
the 34 mm WS-RDN-601 cooler instead of the fitted G48R (the user's call after the thermal test)
the VLP-16 cable shortened to 1 m (the user's call: a Velodyne waiver)
the turret's own: a 24-ball hopper, a one-board bay (its plan, not scheduled here)
the two DCB609 weighed: DeWalt's DCB547-XJ sheet says 1.46 kg against the 1.565 kg (3.45 lb) carried
D69's backup wheel, the 8.5 in of the same family (about 3.3 kg each, unverified): jump +15 mm, kerb 35 mm
two DCB606 FLEXVOLT 6.0 Ah in the same bay and adapters (about 1.0 kg lighter the pair, 2/3 the energy: masses to read from DeWalt)
